lines.text: Welcome to the Stacks, {hero}. I am the Index. I list everything down here, including you, under Pending.
Another reader. How lovely. The last one is filed under Returns. Mind the bin on your way down.
The bookshop closed at six. You did not leave. Bold choice, {hero}. Let us see how it reviews.
Rules of the Stacks: no food, no talking, no surviving. Two of those are negotiable.
Floor {floor}. The air smells of foxing and poor decisions.
Welcome to floor {floor}. Nobody has dusted here since the invention of dust.
Floor {floor}. I would describe it, but you would only skim.
You have reached floor {floor}. Your library card is not valid here. Or anywhere, frankly.
Floor {floor}, {hero}. Deeper than most readers get. Shallower than most readers end up.
Floor {floor}. The stairs behind you have been reshelved. Do not ask where.
Down to floor {floor}. Somewhere above, a customer is asking for a book with a blue cover.
Floor {floor}. My records show you here now. My records also show a cat as head of acquisitions.
This is floor {floor}. It was catalogued once, in pencil, by someone who was clearly crying.
Floor {floor}. Please keep your voice down. Things down here are reading.
A new room. It has been waiting for you, the way a dentist waits.
Note the shelving. Note the silence. Note that I am taking notes.
This room has a five-star rating from one reviewer, who is still in it.
Proceed carefully, {hero}. Or carelessly. I get paid by the obituary either way.
Someone has left a bookmark on the floor. Its owner reached page eleven. Of their life story.
I have cross-referenced this room. It refers you to another room. That one refers you here.
The draught in here is the only plot development for miles.
A sign says Quiet Please. Underneath, smaller: Or Else.
There is a chapter break in the air. Something is about to happen, probably to you.
You have read this paragraph before. Rooms down here reuse their prose. Budget cuts.
This room has been described as atmospheric, mostly by the atmosphere.
Check your pockets. Something down here already did.
I would recommend a different room, but this is the one you have been issued.
Every room is a metaphor, {hero}. This one is a metaphor for a room you may die in.
The light flickers in a pattern. It is Morse code for: overdue.
You are on floor {floor}, in a room, holding your breath. Two of those are sensible.
Somewhere a page turns by itself. Do not look. Looking encourages it.
The previous reader left a review scratched into the wall. It is one word. It is not kind.
Fun fact: this room is load-bearing. So, apparently, is your optimism.
The index card for this room reads: see also, regret. I wrote it in advance.
A six. I had to check it twice. Then I had it laminated.
Magnificent, {hero}. I shall add an asterisk to your entry. A small, grudging one.
That went so well it is almost suspicious. I am opening an inquiry.
Flawless. Somewhere a critic sighs and puts down their pen.
A critical success. Please do not let it go to your head. There is not much room up there.
Excellent. That will be quoted on the back cover, out of context.
A one. Statistically rare. Personally, I saw it coming from the first chapter.
That was a fumble, {hero}. I have filed it under Comedy, subsection Slapstick.
You failed with such commitment that it loops back to art. It does not loop back to success.
Remarkable. You found a way to make it worse that the author never considered.
Oh dear. I will not describe that. I will merely index it, in bold.
If clumsiness were a genre, you would be the anthology.
A strategic retreat. Also known as running, with better publicity.
You flee, {hero}. The monster seems relieved. It had other plans tonight.
Exit, pursued by nothing in particular. Very dramatic.
Cowardice noted. Also survival noted. The two are often filed together.
You leave at speed. Your dignity follows at a more leisurely pace.
And so {hero} was returned, slightly damaged, to the bin. Restocking at the top of floor {floor}.
Dead. Again. I have started a second volume for you.
Cause of death: the plot. Contributing factor: you.
You have died, {hero}. Do not worry, nothing down here stays dead. Except the prose.
Here lies {hero}. Spine cracked, pages loose, marked down to clear.
That was fatal. On the bright side, you are now a cautionary tale. Those sell well.
Deceased. I have updated your status from Reader to Footnote.
The returns bin welcomes you back. It kept your seat warm. It is always warm. Do not ask why.
Oh, {hero}. That ending was rushed. I blame the editor.
Level up. You are now slightly less likely to die. Slightly.
Congratulations, {hero}. You have grown as a person. The monsters have noticed.
A new level. I have moved you from the bargain table to the regular shelf.
You feel stronger, wiser and luckier. Two of those are real. Find out which.
Experience gained. Mostly the experience of nearly dying, which is the best kind.
An achievement. I have added a gold star to your file. It is made of paper. Like everything.
Well done, {hero}. That is now permanent record. So is everything else, unfortunately.
Achievement unlocked. The prize is the feeling. The feeling is non-refundable.
Recognition at last. Frame it. Down here, frames are the only furniture.
Something large is between you and the stairs. It has a title. Titles mean trouble.
This one has a name, {hero}. Things with names have sequels. Try not to be in it.
A guardian of floor {floor}. It has been waiting a long time. It has prepared remarks.
Boss fight. I would wish you luck, but I already wrote the ending, and it is a short one.
A shop. Prices are final. So, often, are the products.
Welcome, valued customer. You are valued at roughly four coins.
Browse freely, {hero}. Shoplifters will be shelved.
All sales are final. All refunds are fictional.
The shopkeeper has been here since the first edition. The stock has been here longer.
Oh. You came back. I had already written your disappearance up as a mystery.
Welcome back, {hero}. Floor {floor} kept your place. It folded the corner, sadly.
